about: Domaine Eden belongs to Mount Eden Vineyards, the Santa Cruz Mountains estate where Martin Ray planted vines on a peak above Saratoga in 1945. Jeffrey Patterson has made the wine there since 1981, and he and his wife Ellie became majority owners in 2008. A year earlier they had bought the neighbouring Cinnabar winery and vineyard, one ridge to the south, founded by Tom Mudd in 1983. They renamed it Domaine Eden and use it for Pinot Noir, Chardonnay and Bordeaux varieties grown a mile from the home estate.

This Pinot Noir is a mosaic of clones and selections: Dijon 777, 667 and 828, alongside the historic California selections Mount Eden, Calera and Swan. It grows on a north-facing slope at about 1,600 feet, dry-farmed for low yields. In 2019 the grapes were picked by hand between September 1 and 19, fermented with native yeasts and aged 11 months in two- to five-year-old French barrels. The wine was neither fined nor filtered.

The importer says Domaine Eden’s different soils give more open varietal fruit and a broader mid-palate than the mineral, shale-grown Mount Eden estate wines. Expect raspberry, anise and a touch of vanilla, with fresh acidity and supporting tannins, in a style that nods to Burgundy. Patterson’s long experience with these mountain clones shows in a Pinot Noir that values balance over sheer power.
